<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="Fix TimeTracking QA gaps">
Fix two accepted QA issues in /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm (story 838, time & pay). You own lib/cleaner_crm/time_tracking*, lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/timesheet_live.ex, and (for the pay fields only) additive edits to lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/job_form_component.ex + job_live.ex.

MCP note: if a tool call errors "No session_id available", add explicit session_id "b82dc084-1093-4624-b490-31c68a31a4a8". If MCP hangs >2 min, message me and continue code work.

Issue 1 — a9233027-786b-4f60-8547-091fb4b85135 (critical): NO UI sets a job's pay_type / hourly_rate_cents / piece_rate_cents (fields exist on Job since the fixture-contract work), so hourly pay, piece-rate pay, running pay-period totals, and payroll CSV export are unreachable through the live product. Fix: add pay fields to the job form (pay type select — its own form wrapper per the phx-change rule if it triggers events — plus rate input(s), dollars accepted and stored as cents), and ensure TimeTracking's Earnings reads them (it already does per the specs). Keep event names/params consistent with existing specs (mix spex 833/834 must stay green).

Issue 2 — e3d5222b-565b-4fae-b0ee-0516ce6319da (high): /timesheets mislabels fully clocked-out jobs as "Missing clock-out", and its Resolve button silently no-ops (KeyError-class bug was previously fixed for rendering; now the RESOLUTION action doesn't work). Debug TimesheetLive's unresolved-entry detection (likely list_job_time_summaries/unresolved? logic vs open entries) and the resolve event handler (form wrapper? event name mismatch?) until: fully clocked-out jobs show as resolved with computed pay, genuinely open entries show the resolve form, and submitting it persists the clock-out and unblocks pay/export.

Verify: MIX_ENV=test mix compile clean, mix spex on 838_*/ + 844_*/ (all green; also 833/834 regression), mix test (all green), mix format. Do NOT run dev-env mix compile or restart the server — the dev server has NO code reloader, so after your fix lands tell me "NEEDS BOUNCE" in your report and I'll restart it for the QA re-run. Call resolve_issue on both ids with fix descriptions (accept flow already done). Final response: files changed, spex/test counts, "NEEDS BOUNCE". Under 150 words.
</teammate-message>

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Clock-in/out per job, hourly and piece-rate pay, transparent
4	  per-job and pay-period earnings, and payroll-ready CSV export.
5	
6	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. Money is
7	  always integer cents; `CleanerCrm.Money` formats it for display and
8	  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings` does the cents math.
9	  """
10	
11	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
12	
13	  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
14	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
15	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
16	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
17	  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.{Earnings, PayRate, PayrollExport, TimeEntry}
18	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.{Scope, User}
19	
20	  ## Clocking in and out
21	
22	  @doc """
23	  Clocks the scope's user in to `job`. Fails closed: `{:error,
24	  :not_assigned}` if the job isn't theirs, `{:error,
25	  {:already_clocked_in, other_job}}` if they're still on the clock
26	  somewhere else.
27	  """
28	  def clock_in(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
29	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
30	    with :ok <- ensure_assigned(job, scope.user),
31	         :ok <- ensure_not_already_clocked_in(scope, job) do
32	      create_time_entry(scope, %{job_id: job.id, clocked_in_at: DateTime.utc_now()})
33	    end
34	  end
35	
36	  @doc "Clocks the scope's user out of their open entry on `job`."
37	  def clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
38	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
39	    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
40	      nil ->
41	        {:error, :not_clocked_in}
42	
43	      entry ->
44	        entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: DateTime.utc_now()}) |> Repo.update()
45	    end
46	  end
47	
48	  defp ensure_assigned(%Job{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}, %User{id: cleaner_id}), do: :ok
49	  defp ensure_assigned(_job, _user), do: {:error, :not_assigned}
50	
51	  defp ensure_not_already_clocked_in(%Scope{user: user} = scope, %Job{id: job_id}) do
52	    case open_time_entry_for_cleaner(scope, user.id) do
53	      nil -> :ok
54	      %TimeEntry{job_id: ^job_id} -> :ok
55	      %TimeEntry{} = entry -> {:error, {:already_clocked_in, Repo.preload(entry, :job).job}}
56	    end
57	  end
58	
59	  @doc """
60	  Creates a resolved (or open, if `clocked_out_at` is omitted or
61	  `nil`) time entry directly. The sanctioned bypass
62	  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.time_entry_fixture` seeds through — real
63	  clock-in/out goes through `clock_in/2` and `clock_out/2` above.
64	  """
65	  def create_time_entry(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
66	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
67	    job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, fetch!(attrs, :job_id))
68	
69	    %TimeEntry{account_id: account_id, job_id: job.id, cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id}
70	    |> TimeEntry.changeset(attrs)
71	    |> Repo.insert()
72	  end
73	
74	  @doc """
75	  Sets the clock-out time on an open entry to a specific time of day
76	  on its clock-in date — how the owner resolves a forgotten
77	  clock-out.
78	  """
79	  def resolve_clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %TimeEntry{} = entry, attrs)
80	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
81	    with {:ok, time} <- parse_time(fetch!(attrs, :clock_out_time)),
82	         {:ok, clocked_out_at} <- combine(entry.clocked_in_at, time) do
83	      entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: clocked_out_at}) |> Repo.update()
84	    end
85	  end
86	
87	  defp fetch!(attrs, key) do
88	    case Map.fetch(attrs, key) do
89	      {:ok, value} -> value
90	      :error -> Map.fetch!(attrs, to_string(key))
91	    end
92	  end
93	
94	  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}
95	
96	  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
97	    case String.split(string, ":") do
98	      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
99	      _ -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
100	    end
101	  end
102	
103	  # Combines the submitted time-of-day with the clock-in's date. A
104	  # resolution submitted for the same day is the common case, but a
105	  # cleaner who clocked in late at night and got resolved the next
106	  # morning would otherwise land before their own clock-in and fail
107	  # validation — so a candidate that doesn't come after clock-in rolls
108	  # forward to the next day instead.
109	  defp combine(%DateTime{time_zone: time_zone} = clocked_in_at, %Time{} = time) do
110	    date = DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)
111	
112	    with {:ok, candidate} <- DateTime.new(date, time, time_zone) do
113	      if DateTime.compare(candidate, clocked_in_at) == :gt do
114	        {:ok, candidate}
115	      else
116	        DateTime.new(Date.add(date, 1), time, time_zone)
117	      end
118	    end
119	  end
120	
121	  ## Reading time entries
122	
123	  def open_time_entry_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
124	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
125	    TimeEntry
126	    |> where(
127	      [t],
128	      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
129	    )
130	    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
131	    |> limit(1)
132	    |> Repo.one()
133	  end
134	
135	  def open_time_entry_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
136	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
137	    TimeEntry
138	    |> where(
139	      [t],
140	      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
141	    )
142	    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
143	    |> limit(1)
144	    |> Repo.one()
145	  end
146	
147	  def list_time_entries_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
148	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
149	    TimeEntry
150	    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id)
151	    |> order_by([t], asc: t.clocked_in_at)
152	    |> Repo.all()
153	  end
154	
155	  ## Earnings
156	
157	  @doc """
158	  Cents earned on `job` so far — see `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings.job_cents/2`
159	  for exactly what that means for each pay type.
160	  """
161	  def job_earnings_cents(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
162	    Earnings.job_cents(job, list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job))
163	  end
164	
165	  @doc "Seconds elapsed on the cleaner's currently-open entry for `job`, or `nil` if not clocked in."
166	  def elapsed_seconds(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
167	    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
168	      nil -> nil
169	      entry -> Earnings.elapsed_seconds(entry)
170	    end
171	  end
172	
173	  ## Pay periods
174	
175	  @doc "The Monday-Sunday week containing `date`."
176	  def pay_period_for(%Date{} = date) do
177	    monday = Date.add(date, -(Date.day_of_week(date) - 1))
178	    {monday, Date.add(monday, 6)}
179	  end
180	
181	  @doc """
182	  The account's current pay period: the week containing its most
183	  recent time entry, falling back to this real-world week when the
184	  account has none yet. Anchoring on the latest activity rather than
185	  the wall clock means newly-seeded or backfilled data is visible the
186	  moment the owner opens the timesheet, with no period picker to
187	  navigate first.
188	  """
189	  def current_pay_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
190	    TimeEntry
191	    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
192	    |> select([t], max(t.clocked_in_at))
193	    |> Repo.one()
194	    |> case do
195	      nil -> Date.utc_today()
196	      clocked_in_at -> DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)
197	    end
198	    |> pay_period_for()
199	  end
200	
201	  @doc """
202	  Every job with time recorded in `period` (a `{start_date, end_date}`
203	  tuple), with its cleaner, entries, earned cents (`nil` if
204	  unresolved), and resolved status — the timesheet's row-level data.
205	  """
206	  def list_job_time_summaries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, {_, _} = period)
207	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
208	    scope
209	    |> time_entries_in_period(period)
210	    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.job_id)
211	    |> Enum.map(fn {_job_id, entries} ->
212	      job = hd(entries).job
213	      cents = Earnings.job_cents(job, entries)
214	
215	      %{
216	        job: job,
217	        cleaner: job.cleaner,
218	        entries: entries,
219	        cents: cents,
220	        # A job counts as unresolved whenever pay can't be computed yet
221	        # (a job missing its pay type entirely leaves `cents` `nil`
222	        # even once every entry is closed — that must block the same
223	        # way an open entry does, not silently price at $0) or whenever
224	        # an entry is still open — piece-rate pays a flat amount
225	        # regardless of entries, so `cents` alone wouldn't catch a
226	        # piece-rate job someone is still clocked in on.
227	        unresolved?: is_nil(cents) or Enum.any?(entries, &(!TimeEntry.resolved?(&1)))
228	      }
229	    end)
230	    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.job.scheduled_date, Date)
231	  end
232	
233	  @doc """
234	  Per-cleaner totals for `period`, excluding unresolved jobs. A
235	  cleaner whose only job is unresolved still appears, at zero — the
236	  amount isn't missing, it's withheld pending resolution.
237	  """
238	  def cleaner_pay_totals(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
239	    scope
240	    |> list_job_time_summaries(period)
241	    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.cleaner.id)
242	    |> Map.new(fn {cleaner_id, summaries} ->
243	      total = summaries |> Enum.reject(& &1.unresolved?) |> Enum.map(& &1.cents) |> Enum.sum()
244	      {cleaner_id, total}
245	    end)
246	  end
247	
248	  defp time_entries_in_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, {start_date, end_date}) do
249	    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
250	    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])
251	
252	    TimeEntry
253	    |> where(
254	      [t],
255	      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.clocked_in_at >= ^start_at and t.clocked_in_at < ^end_at
256	    )
257	    |> preload(job: :cleaner)
258	    |> Repo.all()
259	  end
260	
261	  ## Payroll export
262	
263	  @doc """
264	  Exports `period`'s earnings to CSV, one row per cleaner. Refuses
265	  with `{:error, :unresolved_entries}` while any job in the period is
266	  still missing a clock-out — payroll never goes out on an estimate.
267	  """
268	  def export_pay_period_csv(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
269	    summaries = list_job_time_summaries(scope, period)
270	
271	    if Enum.any?(summaries, & &1.unresolved?) do
272	      {:error, :unresolved_entries}
273	    else
274	      {:ok, PayrollExport.to_csv(summaries)}
275	    end
276	  end
277	
278	  ## Drive-time policy
279	
280	  @doc "The account's drive-time pay policy, for display alongside a cleaner's earnings."
281	  def drive_time_policy(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope)
282	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
283	    Accounts.get_account!(scope, account_id).drive_time_policy
284	  end
285	
286	  ## Pay rates (per-cleaner defaults)
287	
288	  def get_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
289	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
290	    Repo.get_by(PayRate, account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id)
291	  end
292	
293	  def set_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, cleaner_id, attrs)
294	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
295	    scope
296	    |> get_pay_rate(cleaner_id)
297	    |> Kernel.||(%PayRate{account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id})
298	    |> PayRate.changeset(Map.put(attrs, :cleaner_id, cleaner_id))
299	    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
300	  end
301	end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking do
  @moduledoc """
  Clock-in/out per job, hourly and piece-rate pay, transparent
  per-job and pay-period earnings, and payroll-ready CSV export.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. Money is
  always integer cents; `CleanerCrm.Money` formats it for display and
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings` does the cents math.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.{Earnings, PayRate, PayrollExport, TimeEntry}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.{Scope, User}

  ## Clocking in and out

  @doc """
  Clocks the scope's user in to `job`. Fails closed: `{:error,
  :not_assigned}` if the job isn't theirs, `{:error,
  {:already_clocked_in, other_job}}` if they're still on the clock
  somewhere else.
  """
  def clock_in(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- ensure_assigned(job, scope.user),
         :ok <- ensure_not_already_clocked_in(scope, job) do
      create_time_entry(scope, %{job_id: job.id, clocked_in_at: DateTime.utc_now()})
    end
  end

  @doc "Clocks the scope's user out of their open entry on `job`."
  def clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_clocked_in}

      entry ->
        entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: DateTime.utc_now()}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp ensure_assigned(%Job{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}, %User{id: cleaner_id}), do: :ok
  defp ensure_assigned(_job, _user), do: {:error, :not_assigned}

  defp ensure_not_already_clocked_in(%Scope{user: user} = scope, %Job{id: job_id}) do
    case open_time_entry_for_cleaner(scope, user.id) do
      nil -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{job_id: ^job_id} -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{} = entry -> {:error, {:already_clocked_in, Repo.preload(entry, :job).job}}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a resolved (or open, if `clocked_out_at` is omitted or
  `nil`) time entry directly. The sanctioned bypass
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.time_entry_fixture` seeds through — real
  clock-in/out goes through `clock_in/2` and `clock_out/2` above.
  """
  def create_time_entry(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, fetch!(attrs, :job_id))

    %TimeEntry{account_id: account_id, job_id: job.id, cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id}
    |> TimeEntry.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Sets the clock-out time on an open entry to a specific time of day
  on its clock-in date — how the owner resolves a forgotten
  clock-out.
  """
  def resolve_clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %TimeEntry{} = entry, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, time} <- parse_time(fetch!(attrs, :clock_out_time)),
         {:ok, clocked_out_at} <- combine(entry.clocked_in_at, time) do
      entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: clocked_out_at}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp fetch!(attrs, key) do
    case Map.fetch(attrs, key) do
      {:ok, value} -> value
      :error -> Map.fetch!(attrs, to_string(key))
    end
  end

  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}

  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
    case String.split(string, ":") do
      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
      _ -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
    end
  end

  # Combines the submitted time-of-day with the clock-in's date. A
  # resolution submitted for the same day is the common case, but a
  # cleaner who clocked in late at night and got resolved the next
  # morning would otherwise land before their own clock-in and fail
  # validation — so a candidate that doesn't come after clock-in rolls
  # forward to the next day instead.
  defp combine(%DateTime{time_zone: time_zone} = clocked_in_at, %Time{} = time) do
    date = DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)

    with {:ok, candidate} <- DateTime.new(date, time, time_zone) do
      if DateTime.compare(candidate, clocked_in_at) == :gt do
        {:ok, candidate}
      else
        DateTime.new(Date.add(date, 1), time, time_zone)
      end
    end
  end

  ## Reading time entries

  def open_time_entry_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def open_time_entry_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def list_time_entries_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Earnings

  @doc """
  Cents earned on `job` so far — see `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings.job_cents/2`
  for exactly what that means for each pay type.
  """
  def job_earnings_cents(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    Earnings.job_cents(job, list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job))
  end

  @doc "Seconds elapsed on the cleaner's currently-open entry for `job`, or `nil` if not clocked in."
  def elapsed_seconds(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil -> nil
      entry -> Earnings.elapsed_seconds(entry)
    end
  end

  ## Pay periods

  @doc "The Monday-Sunday week containing `date`."
  def pay_period_for(%Date{} = date) do
    monday = Date.add(date, -(Date.day_of_week(date) - 1))
    {monday, Date.add(monday, 6)}
  end

  @doc """
  The account's current pay period: the week containing its most
  recent time entry, falling back to this real-world week when the
  account has none yet. Anchoring on the latest activity rather than
  the wall clock means newly-seeded or backfilled data is visible the
  moment the owner opens the timesheet, with no period picker to
  navigate first.
  """
  def current_pay_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> select([t], max(t.clocked_in_at))
    |> Repo.one()
    |> case do
      nil -> Date.utc_today()
      clocked_in_at -> DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)
    end
    |> pay_period_for()
  end

  @doc """
  Every job with time recorded in `period` (a `{start_date, end_date}`
  tuple), with its cleaner, entries, earned cents (`nil` if
  unresolved), and resolved status — the timesheet's row-level data.
  """
  def list_job_time_summaries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, {_, _} = period)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> time_entries_in_period(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.job_id)
    |> Enum.map(fn {_job_id, entries} ->
      job = hd(entries).job
      cents = Earnings.job_cents(job, entries)

      %{
        job: job,
        cleaner: job.cleaner,
        entries: entries,
        cents: cents,
        # A job counts as unresolved whenever pay can't be computed yet
        # (a job missing its pay type entirely leaves `cents` `nil`
        # even once every entry is closed — that must block the same
        # way an open entry does, not silently price at $0) or whenever
        # an entry is still open — piece-rate pays a flat amount
        # regardless of entries, so `cents` alone wouldn't catch a
        # piece-rate job someone is still clocked in on.
        unresolved?: is_nil(cents) or Enum.any?(entries, &(!TimeEntry.resolved?(&1)))
      }
    end)
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.job.scheduled_date, Date)
  end

  @doc """
  Per-cleaner totals for `period`, excluding unresolved jobs. A
  cleaner whose only job is unresolved still appears, at zero — the
  amount isn't missing, it's withheld pending resolution.
  """
  def cleaner_pay_totals(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    scope
    |> list_job_time_summaries(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.cleaner.id)
    |> Map.new(fn {cleaner_id, summaries} ->
      total = summaries |> Enum.reject(& &1.unresolved?) |> Enum.map(& &1.cents) |> Enum.sum()
      {cleaner_id, total}
    end)
  end

  defp time_entries_in_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, {start_date, end_date}) do
    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])

    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.clocked_in_at >= ^start_at and t.clocked_in_at < ^end_at
    )
    |> preload(job: :cleaner)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Payroll export

  @doc """
  Exports `period`'s earnings to CSV, one row per cleaner. Refuses
  with `{:error, :unresolved_entries}` while any job in the period is
  still missing a clock-out — payroll never goes out on an estimate.
  """
  def export_pay_period_csv(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    summaries = list_job_time_summaries(scope, period)

    if Enum.any?(summaries, & &1.unresolved?) do
      {:error, :unresolved_entries}
    else
      {:ok, PayrollExport.to_csv(summaries)}
    end
  end

  ## Drive-time policy

  @doc "The account's drive-time pay policy, for display alongside a cleaner's earnings."
  def drive_time_policy(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Accounts.get_account!(scope, account_id).drive_time_policy
  end

  ## Pay rates (per-cleaner defaults)

  def get_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.get_by(PayRate, account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id)
  end

  def set_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, cleaner_id, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_pay_rate(cleaner_id)
    |> Kernel.||(%PayRate{account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id})
    |> PayRate.changeset(Map.put(attrs, :cleaner_id, cleaner_id))
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.TimeEntry do
  @moduledoc """
  A single clocked visit to a job: when the cleaner started, and when
  they stopped.

  A `nil` `clocked_out_at` means the entry is open. While the cleaner
  is still on site that's expected and transient; once it's the only
  thing standing between a job and payroll, it's the "missing
  clock-out" the owner must resolve (see
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.resolve_clock_out/3`) before it counts
  toward anyone's pay.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          clocked_in_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          clocked_out_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "time_entries" do
    field :clocked_in_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :clocked_out_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(clocked_in_at clocked_out_at)a

  def changeset(time_entry, attrs) do
    time_entry
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:clocked_in_at])
    |> validate_clock_out_after_clock_in()
  end

  defp validate_clock_out_after_clock_in(changeset) do
    case {get_field(changeset, :clocked_in_at), get_field(changeset, :clocked_out_at)} do
      {%DateTime{} = in_at, %DateTime{} = out_at} ->
        if DateTime.compare(out_at, in_at) == :gt,
          do: changeset,
          else: add_error(changeset, :clocked_out_at, "must be after the clock-in time")

      _ ->
        changeset
    end
  end

  @doc "An entry is resolved once it has a clock-out time."
  def resolved?(%__MODULE__{clocked_out_at: nil}), do: false
  def resolved?(%__MODULE__{}), do: true
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings do
  @moduledoc """
  Pure pay calculations — no scope, no `Repo`. Given a job and its
  time entries, this is the only place clocked time (or a fixed piece
  rate) turns into cents.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.TimeEntry

  @doc "Seconds between clock-in and clock-out. Only meaningful once resolved."
  def worked_seconds(%TimeEntry{clocked_in_at: in_at, clocked_out_at: out_at})
      when not is_nil(out_at) do
    DateTime.diff(out_at, in_at, :second)
  end

  @doc "Seconds elapsed so far on a still-open entry."
  def elapsed_seconds(%TimeEntry{clocked_out_at: nil, clocked_in_at: in_at}) do
    DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), in_at, :second)
  end

  @doc """
  Cents earned on a job given its (possibly empty) list of time
  entries: the flat piece rate regardless of time for a piece-rate job
  — shown even before the cleaner has started, since it doesn't
  depend on any entry existing — or the hourly rate times total
  resolved worked time. `nil` when an hourly job has no resolved
  entries yet, or a job carries neither pay type: there's nothing to
  compute pay from, and it must not be silently priced at $0.
  """
  def job_cents(%Job{pay_type: :piece_rate, piece_rate_cents: cents}, _entries)
      when is_integer(cents) do
    cents
  end

  def job_cents(%Job{pay_type: :hourly, hourly_rate_cents: rate}, entries)
      when is_integer(rate) and is_list(entries) and entries != [] do
    if Enum.all?(entries, &TimeEntry.resolved?/1) do
      entries |> Enum.map(&worked_seconds/1) |> Enum.sum() |> hourly_cents(rate)
    end
  end

  def job_cents(_job, _entries), do: nil

  defp hourly_cents(seconds, rate_cents) do
    Decimal.new(rate_cents)
    |> Decimal.mult(Decimal.div(Decimal.new(seconds), Decimal.new(3600)))
    |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up)
    |> Decimal.to_integer()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.PayrollExport do
  @moduledoc """
  Builds the payroll CSV: one row per cleaner with total hours, job
  count, and gross pay for the period.

  Never called with an unresolved entry still in the set —
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.export_pay_period_csv/2` refuses to build
  one until every job in the period has a resolved time entry.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Money
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings

  @header ["cleaner_email", "hours", "job_count", "gross_pay"]

  @doc """
  `job_summaries` is the list `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.list_job_time_summaries/2`
  returns: one entry per job, each with its `cleaner`, `entries`, and
  earned `cents`.
  """
  def to_csv(job_summaries) do
    rows =
      job_summaries
      |> Enum.group_by(& &1.cleaner.id)
      |> Enum.map(fn {_cleaner_id, summaries} -> cleaner_row(summaries) end)

    [@header | rows]
    |> Enum.map_join("\n", &Enum.join(&1, ","))
    |> Kernel.<>("\n")
  end

  defp cleaner_row([%{cleaner: cleaner} | _] = summaries) do
    total_seconds =
      summaries
      |> Enum.flat_map(& &1.entries)
      |> Enum.map(&Earnings.worked_seconds/1)
      |> Enum.sum()

    hours = total_seconds |> Decimal.new() |> Decimal.div(Decimal.new(3600)) |> Decimal.round(2)
    gross_cents = summaries |> Enum.map(& &1.cents) |> Enum.sum()

    [
      cleaner.email,
      Decimal.to_string(hours),
      Integer.to_string(length(summaries)),
      Money.format_cents(gross_cents)
    ]
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while some spex drive the same form with a
  # `scheduled_date` override instead (matching the schema field name
  # directly). The form carries a second, always-blank
  # `job[scheduled_date]` field purely as a landing pad for that
  # override key (`Phoenix.LiveViewTest.form/3` requires an override's
  # key to match a real field name in the form). Whichever one arrives
  # non-blank wins; `scheduled_date` takes precedence when both do,
  # since a still-blank landing pad means only `date` was ever touched.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"scheduled_date" => sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, "date")

  defp rename_date_key(%{scheduled_date: sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, :date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end

  """

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

    scenario "cleaner forgets to clock out" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the owner attempts to export the pay period containing that job", context do
        {:ok, timesheet_live, html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/timesheets")

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{timesheet_live: timesheet_live, timesheet_html: html})}
      end

            context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.timesheet_live,
                 "[data-test='export-csv-button'][disabled]"
               )

        assert context.timesheet_html =~ "Resolve the unresolved time entry before exporting"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the unresolved job is called out for the owner to fix", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.timesheet_live,
                 "[data-test='unresolved-entry-job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

# Qa Story Brief

## Tool

web

## Auth

Login at http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in (password form, second `<form>` on the
page, id `login_form_password` — the first form is magic-link and shares the same
`user[email]` field name, so scope selectors to `#login_form_password`).

- Owner: `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`
- Cleaner: `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`

Submit buttons are `button` elements with no stable selector other than text
("Log in and stay logged in →"); match by textContent rather than CSS.

## Seeds

Existing QA seed data. Cleaner `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` is user id 2, with
two jobs today (2026-07-08) at /field/jobs/48ae34be-eb88-489b-9bd5-331476a9307b
and /field/jobs/51ef260f-90db-4357-9403-ea3574f9bac2. No job in the dev DB has
`pay_type` set (see Finding below) — none needed seeding for the reachable
scenarios.

## What To Test

- Cleaner clocks in/out of an assigned job (criterion 7121): /field/jobs/:id,
  `[data-test="clock-in-button"]` then `[data-test="clock-out-button"]`.
- Cleaner opens a job not assigned to them (criterion 7123): direct navigation
  to another cleaner's /field/jobs/:id should redirect to /field with flash
  "This job is not assigned to you." and record no time entry.
- Owner reviews /timesheets: pay-period totals, unresolved-entry flagging,
  resolve-clock-out form, CSV export button disabled state (criteria
  7130, 7137, 7140).
- Hourly pay, piece-rate pay, CSV export success path (criteria 7125, 7128,
  7134): **blocked** — see Finding below.

## Result Path

Findings filed via create_issue; outcome via submit_qa_result (this file is
not the canonical record).

## Setup Notes

**Finding, not a config gap**: no page anywhere in the app (job creation, job
edit, or any settings page) exposes `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/
`piece_rate_cents` on a job, and `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.PayRate` (a
per-cleaner default rate) has zero references in `lib/cleaner_crm_web`. Every
job's pay is therefore permanently uncomputable, which cascades into the
timesheet always showing $0.00 totals, every job displayed as "Missing
clock-out" regardless of actual clock state, and CSV export permanently
disabled. Filed as issues a9233027 (critical) and e3d5222b (high). This
blocks 4 of 8 acceptance criteria from being exercised end-to-end; a future
QA pass should re-test 7125/7128/7130/7134 once pay-type entry ships.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story838.Criterion7130Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 838 — Track time and per-job pay in one system
  Criterion 7130 — Running pay-period total builds as jobs complete

  Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec. This
  spec's subject is the running pay-period total across mixed pay
  models, so resolved time entries are seeded directly via
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures` rather than re-driving the clock-in/out
  flow for every job.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the pay-period total grows as each of the cleaner's jobs completes" do
    scenario "running pay-period total builds as jobs complete" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "the account has a cleaner", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "running-total-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, client: client})}
      end

      given_ "the pay period already has an hourly job recorded paying $62.50", context do
        hourly_job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, context.client, %{
            cleaner_id: context.cleaner.id,
            pay_type: :hourly,
            hourly_rate_cents: 2500,
            status: :completed
          })

        Fixtures.time_entry_fixture(context.scope, hourly_job, %{
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 11:30:00Z]
        })

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the owner opens the timesheet for the current pay period", context do
        {:ok, timesheet_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/timesheets")

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{timesheet_live: timesheet_live, timesheet_html: html})}
      end

      then_ "the running total reflects the recorded hourly job", context do
        assert context.timesheet_html =~ "$62.50"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the cleaner completes a second piece-rate job paying $80.00", context do
        piece_rate_job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, context.client, %{
            cleaner_id: context.cleaner.id,
            pay_type: :piece_rate,
            piece_rate_cents: 8000,
            status: :completed
          })

        Fixtures.time_entry_fixture(context.scope, piece_rate_job, %{
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-09 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-09 11:00:00Z]
        })

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the running total grows to include the new job", context do
        {:ok, _timesheet_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/timesheets")

        assert html =~ "$142.50"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story838.Criterion7134Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 838 — Track time and per-job pay in one system
  Criterion 7134 — Owner exports a completed pay period to CSV

  Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec. This
  spec's subject is the payroll CSV export across multiple cleaners,
  so resolved time entries in a closed pay period are seeded directly
  via `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures`.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the owner exports a completed pay period's earnings to CSV" do
    scenario "owner exports a completed pay period to csv" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "three cleaners each have a resolved time entry in a closed pay period", context do
        cleaner1 =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "csv-hourly-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client1 = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job1 =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client1, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner1.id,
            pay_type: :hourly,
            hourly_rate_cents: 2500,
            status: :completed
          })

        Fixtures.time_entry_fixture(context.scope, job1, %{
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 11:00:00Z]
        })

        cleaner2 =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "csv-piece-rate-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client2 = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job2 =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client2, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner2.id,
            pay_type: :piece_rate,
            piece_rate_cents: 8000,
            status: :completed
          })

        Fixtures.time_entry_fixture(context.scope, job2, %{
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })

        cleaner3 =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "csv-hourly-two-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client3 = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job3 =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client3, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner3.id,
            pay_type: :hourly,
            hourly_rate_cents: 2000,
            status: :completed
          })

        Fixtures.time_entry_fixture(context.scope, job3, %{
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner1: cleaner1, cleaner2: cleaner2, cleaner3: cleaner3})}
      end

      when_ "the owner exports that closed pay period to CSV", context do
        {:ok, timesheet_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/timesheets")

        timesheet_live
        |> element("[data-test='export-csv-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {path, _flash} = assert_redirect(timesheet_live)

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :export_path, path)}
      end

      then_ "the CSV has one row per cleaner with hours, job count, and gross pay", context do
        download_conn = get(context.conn, context.export_path)

        [content_type] = get_resp_header(download_conn, "content-type")
        body = response(download_conn, 200)
        lines = String.split(body, "\n")

        assert content_type =~ "csv"

        row1 = Enum.find(lines, &(&1 =~ context.cleaner1.email))
        row2 = Enum.find(lines, &(&1 =~ context.cleaner2.email))
        row3 = Enum.find(lines, &(&1 =~ context.cleaner3.email))

        assert row1 =~ "$50.00"
        assert row2 =~ "$80.00"
        assert row3 =~ "$60.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story838.Criterion7128Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 838 — Track time and per-job pay in one system
  Criterion 7128 — Per-job piece rate pays a fixed amount regardless of time

  Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec. This
  spec's subject is the piece-rate pay calculation, so a resolved time
  entry is seeded directly via `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures` rather than
  re-driving the clock-in/out flow here.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a piece-rate job pays a fixed amount no matter how long it takes" do
    scenario "per-job piece rate pays a fixed amount regardless of time" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a cleaner has a piece-rate job worth a flat $80.00", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "piece-rate-cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            pay_type: :piece_rate,
            piece_rate_cents: 8000,
            status: :completed
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, job: job})}
      end

      given_ "the cleaner completed the job in 2 hours on one visit", context do
        Fixtures.time_entry_fixture(context.scope, context.job, %{
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-09 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-09 11:00:00Z]
        })

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the owner opens the timesheet", context do
        {:ok, timesheet_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/timesheets")

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{timesheet_live: timesheet_live, timesheet_html: html})}
      end

      then_ "the job pays the flat piece rate regardless of hours worked", context do
        assert context.timesheet_html =~ "$80.00"
        refute context.timesheet_html =~ "$160.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

17:- **Always** use the imported `<.input>` component for form inputs from `core_components.ex` when available. `<.input>` is imported and using it will save steps and prevent errors
201:- **Always** use the imported `Phoenix.Component.form/1` and `Phoenix.Component.inputs_for/1` function to build forms. **Never** use `Phoenix.HTML.form_for` or `Phoenix.HTML.inputs_for` as they are outdated
202:- When building forms **always** use the already imported `Phoenix.Component.to_form/2` (`assign(socket, form: to_form(...))` and `<.form for={@form} id="msg-form">`), then access those forms in the template via `@form[:field]`
203:- **Always** add unique DOM IDs to key elements (like forms, buttons, etc) when writing templates, these IDs can later be used in tests (`<.form for={@form} id="product-form">`)
328:        edit_form = to_form(Chat.change_message(message, %{content: message.content}))
335:         |> assign(:edit_form, edit_form)}
345:            <.form for={@edit_form} id="edit-form-#{message.id}" phx-submit="save_edit">
347:            </.form>
433:- Form tests are driven by `Phoenix.LiveViewTest`'s `render_submit/2` and `render_change/2` functions
435:- **Always reference the key element IDs you added in the LiveView templates in your tests** for `Phoenix.LiveViewTest` functions like `element/2`, `has_element/2`, selectors, etc
436:- **Never** tests again raw HTML, **always** use `element/2`, `has_element/2`, and similar: `assert has_element?(view, "#my-form")`
439:- Be aware that `Phoenix.Component` functions like `<.form>` might produce different HTML than expected. Test against the output HTML structure, not your mental model of what you expect it to be
440:- When facing test failures with element selectors, add debug statements to print the actual HTML, but use `LazyHTML` selectors to limit the output, ie:
444:      matches = LazyHTML.filter(document, "your-complex-selector")
447:### Form handling
449:#### Creating a form from params
451:If you want to create a form based on `handle_event` params:
454:      {:noreply, assign(socket, form: to_form(params))}
457:When you pass a map to `to_form/1`, it assumes said map contains the form params, which are expected to have string keys.
462:      {:noreply, assign(socket, form: to_form(user_params, as: :user))}
465:#### Creating a form from changesets
467:When using changesets, the underlying data, form params, and errors are retrieved from it. The `:as` option is automatically computed too. E.g. if you have a user schema:
474:And then you create a changeset that you pass to `to_form`:
478:    |> to_form()
480:Once the form is submitted, the params will be available under `%{"user" => user_params}`.
482:In the template, the form form assign can be passed to the `<.form>` function component:
484:    <.form for={@form} id="todo-form" phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save">
485:      <.input field={@form[:field]} type="text" />
486:    </.form>
488:Always give the form an explicit, unique DOM ID, like `id="todo-form"`.
490:#### Avoiding form errors
492:**Always** use a form assigned via `to_form/2` in the LiveView, and the `<.input>` component in the template. In the template **always access forms this**:
495:    <.form for={@form} id="my-form">
496:      <.input field={@form[:field]} type="text" />
497:    </.form>
502:    <.form for={@changeset} id="my-form">
504:    </.form>
507:- **Never** use `<.form let={f} ...>` in the template, instead **always use `<.form for={@form} ...>`**, then drive all form references from the form assign as in `@form[:field]`. The UI should **always** be driven by a `to_form/2` assigned in the LiveView module that is derived from a changeset

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponentTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent

  # Hosts the component in isolation (no router route required), same
  # pattern as ClientLive.PropertyFormComponentTest. Forwards the
  # component's parent notification to the test process so assertions
  # can use `assert_receive`.
  defmodule Host do
    use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

    @impl true
    def mount(_params, session, socket) do
      {:ok,
       assign(socket, %{
         test_pid: session["test_pid"],
         current_scope: session["scope"],
         action: session["action"],
         job: session["job"]
       })}
    end

    @impl true
    def render(assigns) do
      ~H"""
      <.live_component
        module={JobFormComponent}
        id="job-form"
        current_scope={@current_scope}
        action={@action}
        job={@job}
      />
      """
    end

    @impl true
    def handle_info({JobFormComponent, _} = message, socket) do
      send(socket.assigns.test_pid, message)
      {:noreply, socket}
    end
  end

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp render_host(session) do
    session = Map.put(session, "test_pid", self())
    live_isolated(build_conn(), Host, session: session)
  end

  describe "creating a job" do
    test "renders the job form with the account's properties" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
      property_fixture(scope, client, %{service_address: "12 Oak Lane"})

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      assert html =~ "12 Oak Lane"
      assert html =~ "job-form"
    end

    test "creates an unassigned job and navigates to its show page" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            property_id: property.id,
            date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
            start_time: "09:00",
            end_time: "11:00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

      job_id = path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()
      job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id)

      assert job.property_id == property.id
      assert job.cleaner_id == nil
      assert job.start_time == ~T[09:00:00]
    end

    test "creates a job pre-assigned to a cleaner" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            property_id: property.id,
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
            start_time: "10:00",
            end_time: "12:00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

      job_id = path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()
      job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id)

      assert job.cleaner_id == cleaner.id
    end

    test "rejects a submission missing the required date" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{property_id: property.id, date: "", start_time: "09:00", end_time: "11:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='job-form']")
      assert html =~ "can't be blank" or html =~ "is required"
    end
  end

  describe "assigning a cleaner to an existing job" do
    test "renders the assignment form" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      job = job_fixture(scope, property)

      {:ok, _lv, html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      assert html =~ "assignment-form"
    end

    test "assigns the cleaner when there is no conflict" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: next_tuesday(),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, %Job{} = updated}}
      assert updated.cleaner_id == cleaner.id
    end

    test "rejects the assignment when the cleaner has a time-off block that day" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)
      friday = next_friday()

      availability_block_fixture(scope, cleaner, %{date: friday, all_day: true})

      job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: friday,
          start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
        |> render_submit()

      assert html =~ "conflict"
      assert html =~ "unavailable"
      refute_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, _}}
    end

    test "rejects the assignment when it overlaps another booking for that cleaner" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)
      booking_date = Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)

      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: booking_date,
        start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
      })

      second_job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: booking_date,
          start_time: ~T[11:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[13:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => second_job})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
        |> render_submit()

      assert html =~ "overlap"
      refute_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, _}}
    end
  end

  defp next_tuesday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    offset = Integer.mod(2 - Date.day_of_week(today) - 1, 7) + 1
    Date.add(today, offset + 7)
  end

  defp next_friday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    offset = Integer.mod(5 - Date.day_of_week(today) - 1, 7) + 1
    Date.add(today, offset + 7)
  end
end

content.text: Now I'll implement the fix. First, the `TimeTracking` context needs to distinguish "genuinely missing a clock-out" from "cents can't be computed" (the latter was being conflated into the same `unresolved?` flag, which is why fully clocked-out jobs show "Missing clock-out" and the Resolve button no-ops — there's no open entry for it to act on).

input.old_string:
@doc """
  Every job with time recorded in `period` (a `{start_date, end_date}`
  tuple), with its cleaner, entries, earned cents (`nil` if
  unresolved), and resolved status — the timesheet's row-level data.
  """
  def list_job_time_summaries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, {_, _} = period)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> time_entries_in_period(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.job_id)
    |> Enum.map(fn {_job_id, entries} ->
      job = hd(entries).job
      cents = Earnings.job_cents(job, entries)

      %{
        job: job,
        cleaner: job.cleaner,
        entries: entries,
        cents: cents,
        # A job counts as unresolved whenever pay can't be computed yet
        # (a job missing its pay type entirely leaves `cents` `nil`
        # even once every entry is closed — that must block the same
        # way an open entry does, not silently price at $0) or whenever
        # an entry is still open — piece-rate pays a flat amount
        # regardless of entries, so `cents` alone wouldn't catch a
        # piece-rate job someone is still clocked in on.
        unresolved?: is_nil(cents) or Enum.any?(entries, &(!TimeEntry.resolved?(&1)))
      }
    end)
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.job.scheduled_date, Date)
  end

@doc """
  Every job with time recorded in `period` (a `{start_date, end_date}`
  tuple), with its cleaner, entries, earned cents (`nil` if
  unresolved), and resolved status — the timesheet's row-level data.
  """
  def list_job_time_summaries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, {_, _} = period)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> time_entries_in_period(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.job_id)
    |> Enum.map(fn {_job_id, entries} ->
      job = hd(entries).job
      cents = Earnings.job_cents(job, entries)
      open? = Enum.any?(entries, &(!TimeEntry.resolved?(&1)))

      %{
        job: job,
        cleaner: job.cleaner,
        entries: entries,
        cents: cents,
        # `open?` is genuinely missing a clock-out — the only state a
        # clock-out resolution can fix. `unresolved?` is broader: it
        # also covers a job whose entries are all closed but whose pay
        # can't be computed yet (missing pay type/rate), which must
        # block payroll the same way an open entry does rather than
        # silently price at $0 — but has no open entry for a
        # clock-out resolution to act on, so the two are tracked
        # separately rather than folded into one flag.
        open?: open?,
        unresolved?: is_nil(cents) or open?
      }
    end)
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.job.scheduled_date, Date)
  end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.TimesheetLive do @moduledoc """ The owner's view of a pay period: every job with time recorded, what each cleaner is owed, which entries still need a clock-out before payroll can go out, and the CSV export. Route: `/timesheets`. """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Money alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header> Timesheet <:subtitle> {Date.to_string(elem(@period, 0))} – {Date.to_string(elem(@period, 1))} <:actions> <.button data-test="export-csv-button" phx-click="export" disabled={@unresolved?}> Export CSV

Resolve the unresolved time entry before exporting.

{cleaner.name || cleaner.email}

Pay period total: {Money.format_cents(Map.get(@cleaner_totals, cleaner.id, 0))}

  • {cleaner.email} {Money.format_cents(summary.cents)} Missing clock-out <.form for={@resolve_form} id={"resolve-form-#{summary.job.id}"} data-test={"resolve-clock-out-form-#{summary.job.id}"} phx-submit="resolve_clock_out" > <.input type="time" name="time_entry[clock_out_time]" value="" label="Clock-out time" /> <.button phx-disable-with="Resolving...">Resolve
""" end @impl true def mount(_params, _session, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope period = TimeTracking.current_pay_period(scope) {:ok, socket |> assign(:resolve_form, to_form(%{}, as: :time_entry)) |> assign_period(scope, period)} end defp assign_period(socket, scope, period) do job_summaries = TimeTracking.list_job_time_summaries(scope, period) assign(socket, period: period, job_summaries: job_summaries, cleaners: job_summaries |> Enum.map(& &1.cleaner) |> Enum.uniq_by(& &1.id), cleaner_totals: TimeTracking.cleaner_pay_totals(scope, period), unresolved?: Enum.any?(job_summaries, & &1.unresolved?) ) end defp cleaner_summaries(job_summaries, cleaner) do Enum.filter(job_summaries, &(&1.cleaner.id == cleaner.id)) end @impl true def handle_event("export", _params, %{assigns: %{unresolved?: true}} = socket) do {:noreply, socket} end def handle_event("export", _params, socket) do {start_date, end_date} = socket.assigns.period {:noreply, redirect(socket, to: ~p"/timesheets/export?start_date=#{Date.to_iso8601(start_date)}&end_date=#{Date.to_iso8601(end_date)}" )} end def handle_event("resolve_clock_out", %{"time_entry" => %{"job_id" => job_id} = params}, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id) socket = case TimeTracking.open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do nil -> socket entry -> case TimeTracking.resolve_clock_out(scope, entry, params) do {:ok, _entry} -> assign_period(socket, scope, socket.assigns.period) {:error, _changeset} -> socket end end {:noreply, socket} end end

# The pay-type select and its matching rate input, shared by the
  # `:new`/`:quick_new` and `:edit` forms (`:assign` never touches
  # pay). Only one rate input renders at a time, chosen by the form's
  # current `pay_type` — its raw dollar text lives in `@pay_rate_input`
  # rather than on the changeset, since `hourly_rate`/`piece_rate`
  # aren't real fields on `Job` (only the `_cents` columns are); the
  # dollar amount is converted to cents in `split_pay_params/1` before
  # it ever reaches the changeset.
  defp pay_rate_inputs(assigns) do
    ~H"""
    <.input
      field={@form[:pay_type]}
      type="select"
      label="Cleaner pay type"
      prompt="Not set"
      options={pay_type_options()}
    />
    <.input
      :if={pay_type_value(@form) == "hourly"}
      type="number"
      step="0.01"
      min="0"
      name="job[hourly_rate]"
      id={@form[:hourly_rate_cents].id}
      label="Hourly rate ($)"
      value={@pay_rate_input}
      errors={field_errors(@form[:hourly_rate_cents])}
    />
    <.input
      :if={pay_type_value(@form) == "piece_rate"}
      type="number"
      step="0.01"
      min="0"
      name="job[piece_rate]"
      id={@form[:piece_rate_cents].id}
      label="Piece rate ($)"
      value={@pay_rate_input}
      errors={field_errors(@form[:piece_rate_cents])}
    />
    """
  end

  @impl true
  def update(%{job: job, action: action} = assigns, socket) do
    {:ok,
     socket
     |> assign(assigns)
     |> assign(:conflict_error, nil)
     |> assign(:properties, list_properties(assigns.current_scope))
     |> assign(:cleaners, Scheduling.list_cleaners(assigns.current_scope))
     |> assign(:pay_rate_input, initial_pay_rate_input(job))
     |> assign(:form, build_form(assigns.current_scope, job, action))}
  end

input.new_string:
defp property_options(properties), do: Enum.map(properties, &{&1.service_address, &1.id})

  defp cleaner_options(cleaners), do: Enum.map(cleaners, &{&1.name || &1.email, &1.id})

  defp pay_type_options, do: [{"Hourly", "hourly"}, {"Piece rate", "piece_rate"}]

  defp pay_type_value(form) do
    case form[:pay_type].value do
      nil -> ""
      value -> to_string(value)
    end
  end

  # `hourly_rate`/`piece_rate` aren't real `Job` fields (only the
  # `_cents` columns are), so there's nothing on the changeset to
  # source a freshly-loaded job's dollar display from — this mirrors
  # `with_display_price/1` above, computed straight off whichever
  # `_cents` field matches the job's `pay_type`.
  defp initial_pay_rate_input(%Job{pay_type: :hourly, hourly_rate_cents: cents})
       when is_integer(cents),
       do: cents_to_dollars(cents)

  defp initial_pay_rate_input(%Job{pay_type: :piece_rate, piece_rate_cents: cents})
       when is_integer(cents),
       do: cents_to_dollars(cents)

  defp initial_pay_rate_input(%Job{}), do: ""

  defp cents_to_dollars(cents),
    do: cents |> Decimal.new() |> Decimal.div(Decimal.new(100)) |> Decimal.to_string(:normal)

  # Pulls the submitted dollar rate back out for redisplay (there's no
  # changeset field to read it from, per `initial_pay_rate_input/1`
  # above) and rewrites the matching `job[params]` key to
  # `*_rate_cents` before the changeset ever sees it — clearing the
  # other pay type's rate so switching pay types doesn't leave a
  # stale, unused rate behind.
  defp split_pay_params(%{"pay_type" => "hourly", "hourly_rate" => dollars} = params) do
    {dollars,
     params
     |> Map.put("hourly_rate_cents", dollars_to_cents(dollars))
     |> Map.put("piece_rate_cents", nil)}
  end

  defp split_pay_params(%{"pay_type" => "piece_rate", "piece_rate" => dollars} = params) do
    {dollars,
     params
     |> Map.put("piece_rate_cents", dollars_to_cents(dollars))
     |> Map.put("hourly_rate_cents", nil)}
  end

  defp split_pay_params(%{"pay_type" => ""} = params) do
    {"", params |> Map.put("hourly_rate_cents", nil) |> Map.put("piece_rate_cents", nil)}
  end

  defp split_pay_params(params), do: {"", params}

  # An unparseable dollar amount (or a blank input) becomes `nil`
  # rather than a changeset error — the rate is optional at the schema
  # level, same as `agreed_price`, so an invalid entry is treated as
  # "not set yet" rather than blocking the rest of the form.
  defp dollars_to_cents(dollars) when is_binary(dollars) do
    case Decimal.parse(String.trim(dollars)) do
      {decimal, ""} -> decimal |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
      _ -> nil
    end
  end

  defp dollars_to_cents(_dollars), do: nil

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponentTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent

  # Hosts the component in isolation (no router route required), same
  # pattern as ClientLive.PropertyFormComponentTest. Forwards the
  # component's parent notification to the test process so assertions
  # can use `assert_receive`.
  defmodule Host do
    use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

    @impl true
    def mount(_params, session, socket) do
      {:ok,
       assign(socket, %{
         test_pid: session["test_pid"],
         current_scope: session["scope"],
         action: session["action"],
         job: session["job"]
       })}
    end

    @impl true
    def render(assigns) do
      ~H"""
      <.live_component
        module={JobFormComponent}
        id="job-form"
        current_scope={@current_scope}
        action={@action}
        job={@job}
      />
      """
    end

    @impl true
    def handle_info({JobFormComponent, _} = message, socket) do
      send(socket.assigns.test_pid, message)
      {:noreply, socket}
    end
  end

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp render_host(session) do
    session = Map.put(session, "test_pid", self())
    live_isolated(build_conn(), Host, session: session)
  end

  describe "creating a job" do
    test "renders the job form with the account's properties" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
      property_fixture(scope, client, %{service_address: "12 Oak Lane"})

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      assert html =~ "12 Oak Lane"
      assert html =~ "job-form"
    end

    test "creates an unassigned job and navigates to its show page" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            property_id: property.id,
            date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
            start_time: "09:00",
            end_time: "11:00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

      job_id = path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()
      job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id)

      assert job.property_id == property.id
      assert job.cleaner_id == nil
      assert job.start_time == ~T[09:00:00]
    end

    test "creates a job pre-assigned to a cleaner" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            property_id: property.id,
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
            start_time: "10:00",
            end_time: "12:00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

      job_id = path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()
      job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id)

      assert job.cleaner_id == cleaner.id
    end

    test "rejects a submission missing the required date" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)

Switching pay type clears the other rate's stale cents. TimeTracking.Earnings already read these fields correctly (verified via spex 838/844, all passing with pay set through fixtures); the gap was purely the missing UI. Added regression tests in job_form_component_test.exs covering create-with-hourly, create-with-piece-rate, and edit-to-add-pay-retroactively. Owners can now also retroactively set pay on existing jobs (created before this fix) via the Edit form.

input.resolution: Root cause: TimeTracking.list_job_time_summaries/2 folded two distinct conditions into one `unresolved?` flag (nil cents OR an open entry), so a fully clocked-out job with no pay_type set (the case for every job before issue a9233027's fix) showed "Missing clock-out" and a resolve form that, on submit, hit the `nil -> socket` branch of TimesheetLive's resolve_clock_out handler (open_time_entry_for_job legitimately returns nil since there's no open entry) — a silent no-op, because the real problem was missing pay data, not a missing clock-out. Fix: added a separate `open?` key to each summary (genuinely-open entries only). TimesheetLive now shows the "Missing clock-out" label and resolve form only when `open?`, and a distinct "Pay type not set for this job" message (no dead-end form) when unresolved solely due to missing pay. Once a job has a pay type (via the a9233027 fix) and is fully clocked out, it now renders its computed pay directly. Verified against spex 838 criteria 7137/7140 (missing clock-out + export-blocked scenarios), which exercise the genuinely-open-entry path end-to-end including a real resolve-form submission — all still passing.

content.text:
Both QA issues are fixed and resolved via `resolve_issue`. Summary of the work:

**Root cause (shared by both):** no UI anywhere ever set a job's `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents`, so `Earnings.job_cents` was always `nil`, which made the timesheet's `unresolved?` flag fire for every job — even ones fully clocked out — and the "Resolve" button on those jobs silently no-op'd (there was no open time entry for it to actually resolve).

**Files changed:**
- `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/job_form_component.ex` — added a pay-type select and matching dollar rate input to both the create (`:new`/`:quick_new`) and `:edit` forms, sharing the existing `phx-change="validate"` form. Dollars are converted to cents in the LiveComponent itself so the `Job` schema didn't need touching.
- `lib/cleaner_crm/time_tracking.ex` — `list_job_time_summaries/2` now exposes `open?` (genuinely missing a clock-out) separately from `unresolved?` (blocks pay: nil cents or open).
- `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/timesheet_live.ex` — "Missing clock-out" and the resolve form now only appear when `open?`; a fully clocked-out job with no pay configured gets a distinct "Pay type not set for this job" message instead of a dead-end form.
- `test/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/job_form_component_test.exs` — 3 new tests covering create-with-hourly-pay, create-with-piece-rate, and retroactively adding pay via edit.

**Verification:** clean `MIX_ENV=test mix compile`; spex 838 (8/8), 844 (8/8), and the 833/834 regressions (7/7, 5/5) all green; full `mix test` 160/160; full `mix spex` 100/100; `mix format` clean on everything I touched.

I reported to the team lead with "NEEDS BOUNCE" so they can restart the dev server for QA re-verification, since I didn't touch the dev environment per instructions.
